The supplied passages describe development, scoring and access arrangements, but provide limited evidence about score precision or broader reasoning interpretations. This review applies EFPA 2025 Parts A–C, retaining its item IDs and rating meanings: n/a = inapplicable; 0 = insufficient information; 1 = inadequate; 2 = adequate; 3 = good; 4 = excellent. Section ratings are judgements, not averages. No aggregate quality score is calculated. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; individual authors are not fully listed. Scope: public test problems, official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules; sources inspected 7 October 2026. This is an anonymous AI benchmark-reviewer simulation; current and previous review dates are not supplied.","2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4: Content: rule inference, grid transformation, reasoning. Use: AI comparison and research. Intended test takers: AI systems. Researchers and evaluators are implied users, rather than explicitly specified professional categories.","2.5, 2.9, 2.10, 2.11: One reported benchmark score; no separately established skill scales. Responses are produced grids, judged against target grids. Stimuli are coloured two-dimensional grids with worked examples. There are 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120 problems; problems can contain multiple new inputs.","2.8, 2.12.1, 2.12.2, 2.13: Verified evaluations specify AI settings and spending limits, record conditions and use one run. Reinterpreted administration is evaluation of an individual AI configuration through software; exact hardware and connectivity requirements are unspecified. Other testing routes can differ.","2.15, 2.16, 2.17: Public, semi-private and private sets are distinct fixed evaluation sets, matched for human difficulty. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. Responses come from the assessed AI; this is performance evidence, not human self-report.","3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5: Scoring is digital. Each input earns credit if either of two attempts exactly matches size and every colour. Input credits are averaged within each problem, then problem scores are averaged. The scale is a raw proportion; standard-score transformation is n/a. No differentiated AI norms are described.","5.1, 5.2: Available support includes public problems, development documentation, running software, marking tests, rules and a dated change record. Public data have an Apache 2.0 licence. Hidden-data access is controlled.","6.1.1 = 2; 6.1.3.1 = 2; 6.1.3.2 = 2: The rationale connects unfamiliar example-based transformations to rule inference; task format, low specialist-knowledge aims, developer review and human piloting provide an adequate initial design account. Broader intelligence interpretations remain unestablished.","6.1.3: Development includes newly written and unused earlier puzzles, human piloting, developer review and removal of repeated solution rules. These procedures support deliberate content selection without establishing complete psychometric adequacy.","6.2.1 = 2; 6.2.2 = 2; 6.2.4 = 2: The passages explain the purpose, principal development steps and verified evaluation conditions. Scores support comparison of observed performance on these grid problems under reported conditions.
